observation_summary: The application throws an OutOfMemoryError when processing a large number of weights because it unnecessarily constructs a full n x n matrix from a vector of n elements.
reasoning_summary: The root cause is an inefficient algorithmic choice in how the weight matrix is represented and processed. The code creates a full n x n matrix (1.7 billion elements in the reported case) when only a diagonal representation is needed. This is a procedural/computational strategy error rather than a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability omission (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: When using the Weigth class to pass a large number of weights to multivariate vector optimizers, an nxn full matrix is created (and copied) when a n elements vector is used.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the memory usage is a significant issue, the fix is a local algorithmic optimization (using a sparse or diagonal representation) rather than adding a missing capability or changing the system design.
The issue is not an incorrect initial value, but the choice of an inefficient data structure and algorithm for handling large datasets.
